questions.question: An adult female guppy produces twenty live young in an aquarium. Which characteristic of living things is shown?
options: Living things can move by themselves.
Living things die when they grow old.
questions.explanation: Producing young is an example of reproduction, which ensures the continuity of a species.

questions.question: Which of the following is a non-living thing that can move, but is NOT alive?
options: A snail crawling up a stem
An eagle soaring in the sky
A tadpole swimming in a pond
questions.explanation: A toy helicopter can move, but it cannot grow, reproduce, or respond on its own — it is non-living.

questions.question: Which of the following is the key characteristic of ALL mammals?
options: They have hair or fur and produce milk for their young.
They lay eggs with hard shells.
They breathe through gills when young and lungs when adult.
questions.explanation: All mammals share two key features: they have hair or fur, and they produce milk to feed their young.

questions.question: Which group of animals has dry skin covered with scales and breathes through lungs?
questions.explanation: Reptiles have dry, scaly skin and breathe through lungs throughout their lives.

questions.question: An adult toad can breathe through its lungs on land and through its __________ when in water.
questions.explanation: Amphibians like toads can absorb oxygen through their moist skin when submerged in water.

questions.question: An animal has feathers, a beak, and lays eggs with hard shells. Which animal group does it belong to?
questions.explanation: Feathers, a beak, and hard-shelled eggs are defining characteristics of birds.

questions.question: Which part of a plant traps sunlight to carry out photosynthesis and make food?
questions.explanation: Leaves contain chlorophyll, which traps sunlight energy to carry out photosynthesis and produce food.

questions.question: If strong winds blow against a tree, which plant part prevents it from easily being uprooted from the ground?
questions.explanation: Roots anchor the plant firmly into the soil, helping it resist being uprooted by strong winds.

questions.question: Which of the following animals has a 3-stage life cycle?
questions.explanation: Cockroaches undergo incomplete metamorphosis with a 3-stage life cycle: Egg -> Nymph -> Adult.

questions.question: How is a cockroach nymph similar to an adult cockroach?
options: Both have six legs and three body parts.
Both have the same body size.
questions.explanation: A nymph already resembles the adult cockroach in having six legs and three body parts, but is smaller and lacks fully developed wings.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the pupa stage of a butterfly is correct?
options: It feeds on leaves day and night.
It lays eggs on the underside of leaves.
It does not feed and undergoes transformation inside a cocoon/chrysalis.
It has fully developed wings and can fly.
questions.explanation: During the pupa stage, the insect does not feed and undergoes metamorphosis, transforming into its adult form.

questions.question: During seed germination, which part of the young plant emerges from the seed first?
questions.explanation: The root emerges first during germination to anchor the seedling and begin absorbing water.

questions.question: Which human body system supports the body, gives it shape, and protects delicate internal organs?
questions.explanation: The skeletal system provides support, gives the body its shape, and protects internal organs.

questions.question: The muscular system works closely with the __________ to allow the human body to bend and move.
questions.explanation: Muscles are attached to bones, so the muscular and skeletal systems work together to produce movement.

questions.question: Which of the following shows the correct path of air entering the human respiratory system?
questions.explanation: Air travels from the nose, down the windpipe, and into the lungs where gas exchange occurs.

questions.question: A solid object has a __________.
options: definite shape but no definite volume
definite volume but no definite shape
no definite shape and no definite volume
questions.explanation: Solids have both a fixed shape and a fixed volume, unlike liquids and gases.

questions.question: Which state of matter has no definite shape, no definite volume, and can be compressed easily?
questions.explanation: Gases have no definite shape or volume, and their particles can be pushed closer together, making them compressible.

questions.question: A stone of volume 40 cm^3 is gently dropped into a measuring cylinder containing 60 ml of water. What will the new water level reading be?
questions.explanation: The stone displaces an amount of water equal to its own volume: 60 ml + 40 cm^3 = 100 ml (since 1 cm^3 = 1 ml).

questions.question: Heat always flows from a __________.
options: cooler object to a hotter object
larger object to a smaller object
hotter region/object to a cooler region/object
solid object to a liquid object
questions.explanation: Heat energy always flows naturally from a region/object of higher temperature to one of lower temperature.

questions.question: A metal ball just passes through a metal ring at room temperature. The metal ball is then heated over a flame for five minutes. When placed on the ring again, the ball cannot pass through. Why?
options: The ball expanded when it gained heat.
The ball became heavier when heated.
The ring expanded when it lost heat.
questions.explanation: When heated, the metal ball gains heat energy and expands, increasing in size so it can no longer fit through the ring.

questions.question: Mrs Lee finds it difficult to unscrew a tight metal lid from a glass jar. To loosen the lid easily, she should __________.
options: place the glass jar in a bowl of ice water
dip only the metal lid into a bowl of hot water for two minutes
put both the jar and the lid into the freezer
wrap the metal lid in a cold, damp cloth
questions.explanation: Heating the metal lid causes it to expand more than the glass jar, loosening its grip and making it easier to unscrew.

questions.question: Devi tries to look at a lighted torch through a straight pipe and can see the light clearly. When she bends the pipe in the middle, she can no longer see the light. What property of light does this demonstrate?
options: Light can pass through all materials.
questions.explanation: Since light could not be seen through the bent pipe, this shows that light travels in straight lines and cannot bend around corners.

questions.question: A wooden cylinder is placed between a fixed torch and a screen. To make the shadow on the screen larger, you should move the __________.
options: wooden cylinder closer to the torch
wooden cylinder closer to the screen
torch further away from the wooden cylinder
screen closer to the wooden cylinder
questions.explanation: Moving the object closer to the light source causes it to block a wider spread of light, creating a larger shadow on the screen.

questions.question: Which of the following objects can be attracted by a bar magnet?
questions.explanation: Steel contains iron, which is a magnetic material. Copper, aluminium, and gold are not attracted by magnets.

questions.question: An electromagnet is made by coiling insulated copper wire around an iron nail and connecting it to two batteries. Which change will make the electromagnet stronger?
options: Removing one battery from the circuit
Decreasing the number of coils of wire around the nail
Increasing the number of coils of wire around the nail
Replacing the iron nail with a wooden rod
questions.explanation: Increasing the number of coils of wire around the iron core increases the strength of the electromagnet.
